chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, raising it, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
The Sunnah upon the people of the cities is that they should go out from their cities during the two Eids, except for the people of Makkah, for they pray in the Sacred Masjid.

key_terms.السُّنَّةُ: The established practice or custom, often referring to the Prophetic tradition or a widely accepted legal norm.
key_terms.الْأَمْصَارِ: Cities or large urban centers (plural of Masrah).
key_terms.الْعِيدَيْنِ: The two Eids, referring to Eid al-Fitr and Eid al-Adha.

ai.seo_question: Where should Muslims perform the Eid prayer according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi delineates the spatial jurisprudence of Eid prayers, distinguishing between the general Sunnah of congregating in open fields (Musallas) for urban residents and the specific exception for Mecca’s inhabitants who pray within the Haram. This distinction underscores the unique sanctity of the Sacred Mosque, which serves as both a place of worship and a residence, thereby negating the need to exit the city limits as required elsewhere. The ruling highlights the flexibility in Islamic law regarding prayer locations based on geographical and communal context.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, raising it, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘The Sunnah upon the people of the city is that they should be going out from their cities during the two Eids, except for the people of Makkah, for they would be praying Salāt in the Sacred Masjid’.
en.sarwar: 10. Muhammad ibn Yahya in a marfu‘ manner has narrated from the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
It is of Sunnah for the people of the cities to go out in the open on both ‘Id days except people of Makkah; they perform Salah (prayer) in Masjid al-Haram.’”
